title: Migration Lineage Audit — Production vs Candidate (Product Source SHA 7e063b4)

divergentLineageCollision.description: Two logical migrations were authored under different MigrationIds on the prod-lineage vs the develop/candidate-lineage. Production applied the prod-lineage IDs; the candidate ships the develop-lineage IDs.
divergentLineageCollision.consequenceIfNaiveDeploy: EF MigrateAsync() would treat 20260622140138 and 20260626124527 as PENDING and re-run their Up() → CREATE TABLE on already-existing kpi_template_assignments / report_view_grants → PostgreSQL 42P07 (relation already exists) → migration abort → service fails to start.
divergentLineageCollision.verdict: LINEAGE NOT CLEAN — requires a history bridge (mark the 2 candidate-lineage IDs as already-applied WITHOUT running Up()), identical to the approach already proven on RC (42 rows).

pendingOnProd_perCandidate.outOfOrderNote: 20260620001156_FlexiblePositionsPhase1A has an earlier timestamp than already-applied prod migrations (up to 20260724); EF applies pending in ID order, so it runs first among pending. Must confirm on rehearsal it does not conflict with current prod schema.
pendingOnProd_perCandidate.prodNotInCandidate: none logically new — the only prod-not-in-TEST rows are the two prod-lineage duplicates (20260622144900, 20260626135944), which are the OLD IDs of the same logical migrations

MIGRATION_LINEAGE: NOT_CLEAN — reconciliation (bridge) required; NO-GO until bridge is proven on isolated rehearsal and a written Reconciliation plan is approved.
